title: 175. Combine Two Tables
description:
Write a solution to report the first name, last name, city, and state of each person in the Person table. If the address of a personId is not present in the Address table, report null instead.

Return the result table in any order.
schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE Person (personId INT PRIMARY KEY, lastName VARCHAR(50), firstName VARCHAR(50));
CREATE TABLE Address (addressId INT PRIMARY KEY, personId INT, city VARCHAR(50), state VARCHAR(50));
seed_sql:
INSERT INTO Person VALUES (1, 'Wang', 'Allen'), (2, 'Alice', 'Bob');
INSERT INTO Address VALUES (1, 2, 'New York City', 'New York'), (2, 3, 'Leetcode', 'California');
schema_tables_ascii:
Table: Person

+-------------+---------+
| Column Name | Type    |
+-------------+---------+
| personId    | int     |
| lastName    | varchar |
| firstName   | varchar |
+-------------+---------+
personId is the primary key (column with unique values) for this table.
This table contains information about the ID of some persons and their first and last names.

Table: Address

+-------------+---------+
| Column Name | Type    |
+-------------+---------+
| addressId   | int     |
| personId    | int     |
| city        | varchar |
| state       | varchar |
+-------------+---------+
addressId is the primary key (column with unique values) for this table.
Each row of this table contains information about the city and state of one person with ID = personId.
explanation:
There is no address in the address table for the personId = 1 so we return null in their city and state.
addressId = 1 contains information about the address of personId = 2.
pandas_schema:
data = [[1, 'Wang', 'Allen'], [2, 'Alice', 'Bob']]
Person = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=['personId', 'lastName', 'firstName']).astype({'personId':'Int64', 'lastName':'object', 'firstName':'object'})
data = [[1, 2, 'New York City', 'New York'], [2, 3, 'Leetcode', 'California']]
Address = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=['addressId', 'personId', 'city', 'state']).astype({'addressId':'Int64', 'personId':'Int64', 'city':'object', 'state':'object'})

title: Department Average Salary
description: Calculate the average salary and total employee count per department for departments with at least 2 employees. Round average salary to 2 decimal places.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100), department VARCHAR(50), salary INT);
initial_query: SELECT department, COUNT(*) as employee_count, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) as avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY avg_salary DESC;
solution_sql: SELECT department, COUNT(*) as employee_count, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) as avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY avg_salary DESC;
explanation: Sales has only 1 employee so it is excluded by the HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 condition.

title: Customer Total Order Value (JOIN)
description: Find total spending for each customer who has placed orders. Return customer name and total amount spent.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100)); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT, amount INT);
seed_sql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob'), (3, 'Charlie'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (101, 1, 250), (102, 1, 150), (103, 2, 500);
initial_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) as total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
solution_sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) as total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
explanation: Bob spent 500, Alice spent 250 + 150 = 400. Charlie has placed no orders.
pandas_schema:
customers = pd.DataFrame([[1, 'Alice'], [2, 'Bob']], columns=['id', 'name'])
orders = pd.DataFrame([[101, 1, 250], [103, 2, 500]], columns=['id', 'customer_id', 'amount'])

title: Rank Salaries by Department (Window Functions)
description: Compute the rank of each employee's salary within their department using DENSE_RANK().
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100), department VARCHAR(50), salary INT);
initial_query: SELECT name, department, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) as salary_rank FROM employees ORDER BY department, salary_rank;
solution_sql: SELECT name, department, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) as salary_rank FROM employees ORDER BY department, salary_rank;
explanation: Alice and Bob both have the highest salary in Sales ($70,000) so they share rank 1. Charlie has rank 2.

title: Customers With No Orders (LEFT JOIN)
description: Find all customers who have never placed an order in the database.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100)); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT, amount INT);
seed_sql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob'), (3, 'Charlie'), (4, 'David'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (101, 1, 200), (102, 2, 450);
initial_query: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name ASC;
solution_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name ASC;
explanation: Charlie (id=3) and David (id=4) do not appear in the orders table.

title: Top Selling Products (LIMIT & ORDER)

title: Second Highest Salary (Subquery)
description: Find the second highest distinct salary among all employees.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100), salary INT);
initial_query: SELECT MAX(salary) as second_highest_salary FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);
solution_sql: SELECT MAX(salary) as second_highest_salary FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);
explanation: Highest salary is 120000 (Arun and Ananya). The highest salary below 120000 is 110000 (Priya).

title: Duplicate Email Addresses
description: Find all duplicate emails registered in the users table.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id INT PRIMARY KEY, email VARCHAR(150));
initial_query: SELECT email FROM users GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY email ASC;
solution_sql: SELECT email FROM users GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY email ASC;

title: Active Projects Budget Overview
description: Calculate total budget and project count for each department having active projects.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE projects (id INT PRIMARY KEY, department VARCHAR(50), budget INT, status VARCHAR(20));
initial_query: SELECT department, COUNT(*) as project_count, SUM(budget) as total_budget FROM projects WHERE status = 'active' GROUP BY department ORDER BY total_budget DESC;
solution_sql: SELECT department, COUNT(*) as project_count, SUM(budget) as total_budget FROM projects WHERE status = 'active' GROUP BY department ORDER BY total_budget DESC;
explanation: Engineering has 2 active projects (50000+75000=125000), Marketing has 1 active (45000), Sales has 1 active (20000).

title: Employee Manager Hierarchy (SELF JOIN)
description: Find employees who earn more than their direct managers. Return the employee name and their manager name.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100), salary INT, manager_id INT);
seed_sql: INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Joe', 70000, 3), (2, 'Henry', 80000, 4), (3, 'Sam', 60000, NULL), (4, 'Max', 90000, NULL);
initial_query: SELECT e.name as employee_name, m.name as manager_name FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id WHERE e.salary > m.salary;
solution_sql: SELECT e.name as employee_name, m.name as manager_name FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id WHERE e.salary > m.salary;
explanation: Joe earns $70,000 which is more than his manager Sam who earns $60,000.
